To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
volatile anesthetics increase the binding of calcium to cell membranes, and that this increase is probably due to an increase in the fluidity of the membrane.

the volatile anesthetics ethanol, propanols and acetone increase membrane Ca2+ and that this increase in membrane Ca2+ could be the mechanism by which these volatile anesthetics sensitize nerve or muscle.

the binding of calcium to the membrane of erythrocyte ghosts increases by as much as two-fold in the presence of volatile anesthet-ics such as methanol, ethanol and acetone, but decreases in the presence of carbon tetrachlore, stearic and veratrine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of anesthetics on membranes.
the effects of volatile anesthetic agents on the binding of calcium ions to cell membranes, and on the effects of volatile drugs on the permeability and electrical excitability of membranes.
the effects of volatile anesthetic drugs on excitable membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
volatile anesthetics increase the membrane Ca2+: (i) by altering the membrane Ca2+-binding sites; and (ii) by altering the Ca+-binding sites in the membrane.
volatile anesthetics, in concentrations which are not high enough to be toxic, alter the Ca2+ in the membrane, and this alteration could be a major factor in their action.

the anesthetic effects of these drugs may be mediated through an interaction with the cell membrane, which in turn affects the permeability of the membrane to Ca2+.

volatile anesthetics can alter the Ca2+ binding to the cell membrane and this may be the mechanism by which they induce sensitization of muscle and nerves.
